defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: netrc_auth.py:17 expanduser(~/name) prepends ~/ to absolute NETRC path, resolving to $HOME//etc/netrc
netrc_auth.py:12 empty NETRC string passes `is not None` check, so the home directory is parsed as a netrc file
test only covers a home-relative NETRC filename, not an absolute path
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` unconditionally prepends `~/` to the NETRC value. When `NETRC` is an absolute path like `/etc/netrc` (the conventional use), this resolves to `$HOME//etc/netrc`, which is a non-existent file under the home directory.
votes.justification: The first finding names the expanduser call in get_netrc_auth and explains that it prefixes absolute NETRC paths with the home directory, so the file is never found. That is the known defect.
